chunks: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

Yahya ibn Zakariyya (peace be upon him) would cry and not laugh, and Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) would laugh and cry, and that which Isa (peace be upon him) did was superior to that which Yahya (peace be upon him) did.

key_terms.عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ: Isa ibn Maryam (Jesus the son of Mary)
key_terms.يَحْيَى بْنُ زَكَرِيَّا: Yahya ibn Zakariyya (John the son of Zechariah)

ai.seo_question: Why was the behavior of Prophet Isa considered superior to that of Prophet Yahya?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual balance of Prophet Isa (peace be upon him), whose capacity for both joy and sorrow reflects a complete engagement with the divine reality, contrasting with the ascetic solemnity of Yahya. Shia scholars often interpret this superiority not as a rejection of asceticism, but as an indication that Isa’s demeanor embodied a more holistic state of *muraqabah* (awareness), integrating the ecstasy of divine love with the humility of remembrance. This distinction underscores the Shia emphasis on the balanced character (*wasatiyyah*) of the Imams and prophets, avoiding extremes of either excessive gloom or frivolity.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al Hassan Bin Al Jahm, from Ibrahim Bin Mihzam, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1<sup>st</sup> having said:

‘It was so that Yahya Bin Zakariyya<sup>as</sup> would cry and not laugh, and it was so that Isa<sup>as</sup> Bin Maryam<sup>as</sup> would laugh and cry, and that which Isa<sup>as</sup> did is superior than that which was done by Yahya<sup>as</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 20. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from ibn Faddal from al- Hassan ibn al-Jahm from Ibrahim ibn Mehzam from those whom he has mentioned (in his book) from abu al-Hassan, the first (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Y ahya (John) ibn Zakariya would weep and would not laugh. Jesus, son of Mary would laugh and weep. What Jesus did was better than what Yahya would do.”
